report: The renal tissue section displays cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and round nuclei, some with prominent nucleoli, suggesting cellular activity. Disrupted architecture and mononuclear cell presence indicate a potential inflammatory process. Lacking clear tubular or glomerular structures, with mildly expanded interstitium, features suggest interstitial nephritis or other renal pathology, pending further clinical and molecular evaluation for precise diagnosis.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Decision tree for pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features versus metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma
evidence.text: A decision tree using TTF-1, SATB2, CDX2, and CK7 was developed to distinguish primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with mucinous features from metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma. The validation results support using multiple markers and clinical context when assigning a primary site.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

review.assessment: The vision models provide conflicting classifications (prostate adenocarcinoma, kidney renal clear cell carcinoma, lower-grade glioma) that are not supported by the provided pathology report.
rationale: The de-identified report describes renal tissue with eosinophilic cytoplasm and mononuclear cells suggesting interstitial nephritis, which does not align with the clear cytoplasm and chicken-wire vasculature characteristic of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.
The report explicitly states a lack of clear tubular or glomerular structures, contradicting the glandular architecture required for the adenocarcinoma labels suggested by CONCH, MUSK, and PLIP.

None of the retrieved literature [PMID:26447895, PMC:7944528-SkinCancerMorphology, PMID:26137020, PMID:37676090, PMC:3418538-ColorectalMorphology] provides evidence supporting the model outputs based on the report's description of inflammatory renal pathology.
discrepancies: Vision models suggest malignancy (adenocarcinoma, glioma), whereas the report suggests an inflammatory process (interstitial nephritis).
CONCH suggests kidney renal clear cell carcinoma, but the report describes eosinophilic cytoplasm rather than clear cytoplasm.
recommended_review: Human pathologist review to reconcile the inflammatory description in the report with the malignant classifications of the vision models.
Molecular evaluation as suggested in the report for precise diagnosis.
limitations: The retrieved literature focuses on lung and colorectal differentials and does not address interstitial nephritis or the specific renal morphology described.
